Jafar Alim Khan with Sanzida Akter Khan, Advocates—For the Appellant. 
Md Monzur Rabbi Advocate—For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Vergon Tobacco represented by its Proprietor Raisul Haque Mohammad Defendant-Appellant
VS
British American Tobacco Bangladesh Company Limited and another……….Respondents
full_judgment:
This appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 13-3-2019, passed by the learned District Judge, Kushtia, in Title Suit No. 1 of 2019, allowing the application filed under Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, whereby the defendant was restrained from producing, marketing and selling their Cigarette brand named "PURBANY" on the prima-facie ground of passing off. 

 2. The plaintiff British American Tobacco Company's case, in brief are that, they have manufactured their product Cigarettes and have been marketing and selling the same under the name "DERBY" in a packet having distinct feature and their trade mark 'has been registered on 19-12-2012, but the defendant Vergon Tobacco has begun to manufacture and is selling in the market the similar product by imitating the look of their packets, with the motive which constitutes an act of passing off of the product of the plaintiff. Accordingly, they have prayed for permanent injunction for restraining the defendant from manufacturing, marketing and selling their Cigarettes named "PURBANY" by imitating the same colour, design and look of their packets. The trial court, having heard the parties, by the impugned judgment and order dated 13-9-2019, had allowed the application for injunction. Being aggrieved by that order, the defendant has preferred this appeal. 

 3. Learned Advocate Ms Sanzida Akter Khan appeared for the defendant-petitioner and submits that, the petition for temporary injunction filed by the British American Tobacco Company Bangladesh Limited, against Vergon Tobacco and 2 (two) others seeking permanent injunction as well as mandatory injunction is not maintainable as per law in as much as the authority to address the grievance in this case as well as the power of registration and refusal of trade mark lie in the Registrar of the Trade Mark, but the plaintiff did not lodge any complain, nor had raised any objection to the Registrar of the Trade Mark. She also submits that, without doing so, the plaintiff has directly come before this Court and, as such, this plaint is pre-matured and the civil court lacks jurisdiction to try this suit. Hence, the order of injunction is without jurisdiction. The learned Advocate has mainly relied upon the provisions of section 10, sub-section 2(3) as well section 18 of the Trade Mark Act, 2009 to support her contention. 

 4. Learned Advocate Mr Md Monzur Rabbi appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party. He, on the contrary, submits that, this suit is not pre-matured and, apparently, causes of action having arisen for filing suit, therefore, the plaintiff was constrained to file the same, as permitted by section 96 of the Trade Mark Act, 2009. He has relied upon the decision, reported in 54 DLR 394; between Abdul Mannan Miah vs Md Salaiman Miah as well as some other foreign judgments to support his contention that the order of temporary injunction has been passed by a competent court and in an appropriate case. He concludes that, this appeal bears no merit and the same may kindly be dismissed. 

 6. From the documents annexed to the application for vacating the order of stay, I find that, the trade mark of the cigarettes manufactured by the plaintiff-respondent has been registered on 19-12-2012, in class 34, under No. 160113, vide Annexure-2 to the application for vacating the order of stay. I also find that, there are similarities (so far as the colour, design and size are concerned) between packets of both cigarettes and the similarity tends to deceive the consumer group, who smokes these kind of cigarettes, having similarity in prices too. Besides, the word "DERBY" used in the packet used by the plaintiff and the word "PURBANY" used by the defendant is visually similar. The names of the Cigarettes are written in English on the packets and the spelling and the phonetic difference could be noted only by the person literate in English. 

 9. I have noted the principle and the law, relied upon by the plaintiff, for disposal of this matter. In the case of Nasir Miah Malik Nasir Soan Factory vs Md Anwar Hossain, Executive Officer, Commander Soap Factory Limited, reported in 48 DLR 28, it has been held that, the word "MOSCO (মসকো)" used in the soap packet of the defendant is phonetically and visually similar to the word "COSCO (কসকো)" used by the plaintiff in the packet of the soap and can create doubt and deceive and the defendant used similar colour and design of the plaintiff for the said purpose and, as such, plaintiff has prima-facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is in his favour and it would suffer irreparable loss and injury (if no injunction is granted). 

 12. As such, having considered the facts as well as the provisions of the Trade Mark Act, 2009, and the decisions referred above, I am of the opinion that, the court below has committed no error of law. I also find that, there is a prima-facie case for passing the impugned judgment and order dated 13-3-2019, by the District Judge, Kushtia, and that, the balance of convenience and inconvenience was in favour of granting injunction. On these points, I find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order dated 13-3-2019. 

 I find that, the trademark of the defendant-appellant has not yet been registered. On the other hand, the trademark of the plaintiff-respondent-opposite party has already been registered under the Trade Mark Act, 2009. This is a trademarks dispute. Therefore, let this application for vacating the order of stay be kept with the record and the other side is directed to get this appeal heard within 15-11-2019, otherwise, the order of stay shall stand vacated". 

 15. Alongside, the learned Advocate for the opposite party has brought to the notice of this Court that, during pendency of this appeal, the defendant has been marketing similar Cigarettes in a different way, that is only by changing the name from "PURBANY" to "PUREBANY" and the plaintiff was compelled to file another Civil Suit No. 3 of 2019 before the District Judge, Kushtia, in which an ad-interim order has been passed by the trial court, on 19-9-2019.
